note: The controlled direction vocabulary (D96, p004). A word that names an intent in a proposal, a ruling's because clause, a pose sheet or a material must be a term here (or an alias in the project's overrides). Terms are project-agnostic; a film's own words go in its vocabulary-overrides.json. A word that appears under two domains has one entry whose definition carries both senses.

accent.definition: The one local hue beside the radiance.

action.definition: The main move between two keys.

anticipation.definition: A small opposite move before the action that announces it.

body-gap.definition: A gap between the body and an arm that frames something behind it.

bounce.definition: Light returned from a lit surface to what is near it.

breakdown.definition: A drawing between two keys that fixes the path the move takes.

centre.definition: Subject on the frame's middle line; stable and formal.

close.definition: A face or a single hand fills the frame.

comic.definition: Timing built for a gag: set-up, beat, pay-off.

cone.definition: Light bounded to a beam with a clear edge.

contentment.definition: Nothing is needed; the end state.

crisp.definition: Edges hold their shape; short settle, little boil.

crossing.definition: The film's passage between worlds: reduce to lines, re-route, refill.

curiosity.definition: The light or move invites a closer look.

cut.definition: The picture changes on one frame.

doorway.definition: Subject framed by an opening; a threshold is near.

drape.definition: Hangs and folds under its own weight; cloth and cloak.

drift.definition: A slow unmotivated float of a few pixels; the frame breathes.

dutch.definition: A tilted horizon; the world is off balance.

edge.definition: Subject pushed to the frame's rim; tension or smallness.

emitter.definition: The object that gives off the beat's light.

even.definition: Equal spacing between drawings; mechanical, the named failing control.

extreme wide.definition: The figure is a speck and the place is the subject.

eye.definition: Camera at the subject's eye line; neutral, shared.

falling.definition: Intensity or grain dropping across the beat.

favour.definition: Which key a breakdown sits nearer, as a fraction of the way.

fill.definition: A weaker light that lifts shadows and lowers contrast.

float.definition: Slow arrival with a long ease. As material.intent: high drag and a long lag.

flood.definition: Light that fills the frame or the whole field.

focus.definition: Attention narrows and the rest recedes.

grip.definition: A hand closes on an object; commitment.

high.definition: Camera above looking down; the subject shrinks. As staging: subject high in the frame; lift or exposure.

hold.definition: A drawing stays unchanged for a count of frames.

identity pigment.definition: Codex blue and Clawd coral; never graded.

insert.definition: An object or detail alone, cut in to show what the figure attends to.

inviting.definition: Open poses and a beckoning rhythm; come in.

key.definition: The main light; the brightest thing on the subject.

lag.definition: The light arrives after the thing that causes it. As a secondary: the frames a part trails its primary.

lean in.definition: The body tips toward something; interest.

lift.definition: Raising an object or oneself; effort, then release.

lit-paper.definition: A paper-coloured field lit by the beat's light, not black.

locked.definition: No camera motion for the whole shot.

look through.definition: The gaze goes through an opening to what lies beyond.

low.definition: Camera below looking up; the subject grows. As staging: subject low in the frame; weight, sitting, being small.

medium.definition: The figure from the waist up; gesture and face share the frame.

medium close.definition: Chest up; the face carries and the hands still enter.

medium wide.definition: The figure from head to knee with room around it.

memory.definition: The light keeps a trace after its source has moved on.

morph.definition: One shape becomes another by deforming.

motivated.definition: Light whose direction has a source inside the world.

moving hold.definition: A hold that keeps a few pixels of drift or a face change so it stays alive.

narrow.definition: A tight cone around one thing.

negative-space.definition: A large empty field around the subject; quiet or isolation.

neutral.definition: No colour added; the default when nothing is asked.

noisy.definition: Grain and flicker in the light; trouble or busyness.

nudge.definition: A small push from a companion; help or a gag.

on ones.definition: A new drawing every frame; the film's light layer.

on twos.definition: A new drawing every second frame; the film's drawn layer.

overhead.definition: Camera straight down; the scene reads as a plan.

overshoot.definition: The move passes its target and returns.

overwhelm.definition: More arrives than the figure can take in.

pair.definition: Two subjects balanced or linked by a line between them. As colour: a beat's two hues: its radiance and its accent.

pan.definition: The camera swings sideways about a fixed point.

passing position.definition: The off-line drawing a body passes through mid-move, giving the move an arc.

playful.definition: Light, quick and willing to be silly.

pov.definition: The frame is what a character sees.

practical.definition: A light source that is visible in the frame.

pull.definition: The camera travels away; reveal or release.

pulse.definition: A rhythmic swell of the light on a beat.

push.definition: The camera travels toward the subject; emphasis and commitment.

push-through.definition: The camera or figure passes through a surface into the next place.

radiance.definition: The hue the light gives the field.

reach.definition: An arm extends toward something; wanting.

reduce-to-lines.definition: A picture gives up its fills until only contour remains.

refill.definition: Colour returns into a line drawing.

reverent.definition: Slow, still and held; the moment is large.

rim.definition: An edge light that separates the subject from its field.

rising.definition: Intensity or grain climbing across the beat.

satisfaction.definition: A thing works and the figure knows it.

seam.definition: Light escaping along a join between two things.

settle.definition: The decay to rest after the action stops.

settled.definition: Steady intensity and grain across the beat.

slump.definition: The body gives way; defeat or fatigue.

snap.definition: Fast arrival with a short ease. As material.intent: low drag and a short settle.

soft.definition: A feathered shadow edge. As material.intent: feathered shadow stipple and high diffusion.

staggered.definition: Parts arrive on different frames instead of one.

step.definition: Weight passes from one foot to the other.

still.definition: Does not move unless something moves it; no idle motion.

swell.definition: Size or light rises to a peak, then the change happens.

tense.definition: Tight holds and short, sharp moves; something may go wrong.

third-left.definition: Subject on the left third line; room to look into.

third-right.definition: Subject on the right third line; room to look into.

threshold.definition: The moment of crossing an opening; the commitment point.

tilt.definition: The camera swings up or down about a fixed point.

tower.definition: A tall vertical stack; scale and ascent.

turn.definition: The body rotates to face a new direction; a decision.

volume.definition: Light as a bounded body in the space, not a surface shading.

warm.definition: Friendly and close; the world is glad to see you.

weighted.definition: Mass shows: it lands and settles, and what it carries swings after it.

whip.definition: A fast pan that smears into the next shot.

wide.definition: The whole place with the figure's full body, small in it.

window.definition: Subject framed by a lit opening; looking in or out.

wonder.definition: Something large and beautiful is allowed to be seen.
